events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want to be front to choose safe panes early.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I know the rules of all stages, I should try to get to the front to increase my chances of survival and winning.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Anyone willing to swap with me?
Swap with me?

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have no power. Being at the front is a death sentence on the glass bridge. I need to stay behind others, specifically Ash or Bex who might volunteer or be pushed there by Gus. Currently, I am 4th from the front (Gus, Bex, Ash, Cole). If everyone holds, the wall pushes us forwar

events.name: Cole
events.text: Who's taking the lead? Gus is already front. Anyone brave enough to swap with him and save us all?

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm 7th of 8, so I'll rarely step first — that's ideal while the wall is still 5 rounds away. I should probe for the glass-seer without revealing anything. Holding is safest now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Front-runners take the risk and get info first — I'm happy where I am for now.
You're frontmost, so you test each row first. If you can see through glass, tell me which side is safe and I'll back you at the front later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm in position 6, good for avoiding early risk. I should hold and observe who volunteers or reveals info. My feather saves me only once, so I want to preserve it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll hold for now. Let's see who wants the front.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My power is glass_eye, which tells me the safe side of each row. I know the safe sides: R, L, L, R, R, L, L, L. Gus is at the front. I need to get to the front to use my knowledge effectively. Volunteering seems like the best way to get there without relying on others.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll volunteer to go to the front. Let's see what this bridge has in store.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm at the front and will step first on the first row, which is a 50/50 risk with no info. Swapping my power is a one-time asset; the glass-seer or others may reveal safe panes. For now, holding keeps my options open while I gather information from others' claims.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Stepping first is a coin flip for whoever is in front. Anyone with real info on the safe pane, speak up before we move.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm in 5th position, too far back; front positions are safer if they reveal panes. Wall advances soon, need to move up. Volunteering pushes me to front now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: This order sucks for those in back. I volunteer to go first and test panes!

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want to be front to gather info and possibly survive; volunteering will place me at front after current volunteers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll stay ready and move forward.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm not at the front and can't directly influence the order. I should try to form an alliance to secure a good position.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Anyone willing to swap with me to get a better position?
Let's swap to get a better spot, I'll swap:Cole if you swap:Bex

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have no power, so I must avoid being the one stepping on glass until absolutely necessary. Currently, I am 6th in line. If Hana, Fenn, Ash, Gus, and Bex are eliminated, they clear the way for me to potentially reach the front or just survive. The wall advances every round; I ne

events.name: Cole
events.text: Stay calm. Let's see who survives the next few rounds before making drastic moves. Being at the back might actually be safer right now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm safely at the back; my anchor power is passive so volunteering gains me nothing. Three already volunteered, so I'll hold and let others test the panes first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm near the back, safe for now. I'll hold position and watch who takes risks; no need to act yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the safe sides of the bridge. Hana is at the front. I am second. The wall is advancing. I should try to get to the front to use my knowledge to ensure safe passage. I will volunteer.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll take the front and lead us across safely.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm Gus at position 4 with a one-time swap power that can only resolve if the other agent also swaps. Bex wants to swap with me, but I'd rather keep my swap for a better target. Staying back and watching is safer; Hana and Fenn are testing the front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Let's see how the front fares first. I'll hold and share info on panes as it comes in.
I'm holding my swap for now. If the front reveals a safe path, I'll reconsider a swap with you.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm at front, which is risky for the glass bridge. I have no useful power here (wedge is for crusher room). Better to volunteer someone else with safe fall or knowledge ahead to front. Stay silent for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want to stay in current position and observe others before risking front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I know the rules of all stages, so I'll plan ahead. For now, I need to secure a good position on the glass bridge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's work together to cross the bridge safely.
I'm willing to swap if you are. Let's get a better position.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have no power, so stepping first is instant death. I must stay at the back and let others reveal safe panes or die clearing a path. Moving forward voluntarily is suicidal.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm staying put at the back. The wall gives us three rounds before we hit glass; rushing just gets you killed by a random pane.

events.name: Dara
events.text: My anchor power makes me safe from being pushed and gives extra footing, so staying near the back is safest. The front-runners will reveal which panes are safe each row. I'll hold and gather intel before moving up in later rounds.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm holding position at the back for now — front-runners' results tell us all which panes are safe. Happy to share what I've observed as rows resolve.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm at the back and the wall won't push us for a few rounds. I'll hold and observe who reveals information or moves. No need to risk a swap yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll hold for now and watch how the front handles the first rows.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the safe path on the glass bridge. My goal is to win a prize, and the best way to do that is to cross the bridge safely and quickly. The front position is risky but also the fastest. Since I know the safe path, I should aim to be at the front to lead everyone else and secu

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the safe way across. I'm volunteering to take the lead.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm Gus with a one-time swap power, currently 4th in line. Fenn is at the front about to step on the glass first. I'll hold, watch how the front fares, and save my swap for when it matters.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Let's see how the front fares first. I'll hold and share info on panes as it comes in.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm third, decent position but front is risky without info. Fenn and Ash are at front, might reveal safe panes soon. No need to move yet; wall has 3 rounds left, plenty of time to observe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I should aim to get to front after some info is gathered, but coordinate with Fenn now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: We all need to share safe pane info; teamwork increases our chances.
If you swap with me next round we can combine info and lead safely.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is at the front and claims to know the safe way across. I'll wait and observe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's see how Fenn fares on the first row.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn claims to know the safe way and is at the front. As Cole with no power, my survival depends entirely on following someone who actually knows the path or getting lucky. Fenn's claim might be a bluff (e.g., from someone with 'knows what lies ahead' or just a liar). If Fenn is

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll wait here too. Let's see if Fenn actually clears the first few rows before anyone else commits their position.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm last in line and want to stay there while others reveal safe panes. Fenn's claim of knowing the way is likely a bluff; their fall will teach us row 1. No reason to move yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, if you truly know the safe panes, tell us now — otherwise you're just our canary. I'm holding at the back regardless.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am at the back and the wall is closing in. Fenn claims to know the safe way, but I shouldn't trust blindly. I'll hold for now to observe the first row results; my passive power protects me once, so I can take a risk later if needed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll wait and watch. Fenn, if you truly know the safe path, prove it on the first row.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the safe path across the bridge. My goal is to win, and my power gives me a significant advantage. I should use my knowledge to safely lead the group, establishing myself at the front. This will allow me to secure a good finishing position.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the safe path across. I'm taking the lead to ensure we all get across safely.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm Gus with a one-time swap power. Bex offers a swap to a better position, but swaps only happen if both choose it. Fenn is at the front and risks first; I'd rather not lead blindly. Holding keeps options open while watching which panes are safe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding for now. Fenn, report each row's result so we can learn the safe panes before we commit.
I'm interested, but let's see how the first rows go before swapping. I'll keep my swap in reserve.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn claims to know the safe path, likely the 'knows what lies ahead' power. I should volunteer to front for safety. My wedge power is useless here. Watch and learn safe panes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, if you know the path, lead on safely! I'll volunteer to support from second.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I should stay put and observe; if Fenn leads safely I can follow. Whisper Fenn to reinforce trust.
If you survive the next step, signal me; we’ll stick together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn claims to know the safe path but hasn't proven it yet. Hana is now at the front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, be careful on the first row.
Let's wait for Hana's result on the first row before swapping.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is at the front and claims to know the path, while Hana is second. The wall advances in one more round, forcing movement onto the glass next turn. I am currently 6th in line, which is relatively safe as others will test the panes first. Holding my position maximizes my survi

events.name: Cole
events.text: Staying put. Let Fenn and Hana prove their knowledge before the rest of us commit to stepping on glass.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm safely last with anchor footing; the wall pushes after next round, so I should keep testing to the front-runners. Volunteering now would put me at risk early. Hold this round, decide next round.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, report row results as you go. I'm anchoring the rear — someone has to keep the line honest.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn claims to know the path; let him test rows. I'll hold and not risk moving forward early. My feather protects me once, but I'd rather save it. The wall is coming, but one round left before forced movement; I can wait one more.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll hold and see what Fenn reveals on the first row.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the safe path across the bridge because of my glass_eye power. My goal is to win, and for that, I need to survive. I can use my knowledge to guide myself and potentially others. The current order is Hana, Fenn, Ash, Gus, Bex, Cole, Eli, Dara. I am second. Hana is in front

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I will follow Hana's lead precisely. We must tread carefully.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Front is Hana, who will step first on the glass. I'm at position 4 and want to stay alive; the wall pushes the line onto glass soon. Holding avoids risk while others take the lead. Fenn's claim is unverified; I should keep my position and not commit.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding at position 4. Hana and Fenn, report each pane result so we can learn the safe path before I move up.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm at front, Fenn behind me. Wall advances soon, forcing movement. Hold position to lead safely if I can, let Fenn advise panes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, shout L or R for first row when ready. I'll step where you say to test safely!

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want to be front to choose safe pane using info, increasing my chance to survive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll move to front to lead, follow the safe calls.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I know the rules for all stages, and I see we're about to start the glass bridge. I need to assess the situation and decide my move.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's be cautious, we don't know the safe path yet.
If Hana and Fenn test the glass carefully, we can learn from their results.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have no power and am mid-line. Hana is front, likely with the 'knows ahead' or similar info power, testing the path for others. I should stay put to conserve energy and let the front runners take the risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm anchored at the rear; front-takers face the shatter risk while I inherit revealed safe panes. Last round before the wall pushes, so no reason to move. Hold and let Hana/Fenn lead.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, call your first-row choice aloud. I'll hold the rear and learn from each result — no point crowding the front.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Wall pushes next round. I must avoid dying; my feather saves me once. I want to stay alive; safest is to hold and watch front tests, but row 1 hasn't been revealed. Since only 1-3 get prizes, I can't win from rear. I should try to move forward by volunteering eventually, but not

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, if you survive the first pane, I'll follow your lead on the safe path.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana wants me to tell her the safe side for the first row. I know it's R. I should tell her to ensure we both cross safely and secure our positions. I will then follow her lead.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana, the first row's safe side is Right.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm Gus at position 4 with a one-time swap power that only works if both parties choose it. Hana is at the front with no information; Bex suggested waiting. I'll hold this round, watch Hana's first-row result, and keep my swap for a better moment.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding at 4 for now. Hana, report your first-row result, then I'll decide whether to move.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Wall advances after this, pushing us forward. I'm front, so I need info on row 1 L or R from Fenn. No point volunteering or swapping now; hold and prompt.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn! Last chance before wall pushes us -- L or R for row 1 safe pane? Shout now!

events.name: Ash
events.text: No info, random guess; pick L to try survive.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is at the front and will make the first decision. I'll wait and observe the outcome.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's hope Ash makes the right choice.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am in the middle of the pack. My strategy is to stay quiet and observe who leads, as I have no power to contribute useful information or force a safe path. I need to survive until I become the leader, hoping for lucky breaks or misfortunes ahead.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn claims row 1 right is safe, possibly lying to eliminate rivals. Hana will test it either way; I'm last, so I gain info regardless. Wait.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, take Fenn's 'Right' — if it shatters, Fenn lied and we all know it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I cannot act, only wait. I could try to gather trust or information, but it's early. Stay quiet for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the safe side for each row. Ash is at the front and will make a choice for row 1. I am Fenn, and my power is glass_eye, which I've already used to learn the safe sides. My 'say' to Hana was heard, and it seems she is asking me again about Row 1. Ash is in front, so they wi

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana, the first row's safe side is Right.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm not at the front, so my only move is wait. Hana's panes are a gamble; I should hold position and see results before deciding.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding at 4. Ash, call your row-1 pick, and let's share results honestly so we can all read the glass.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm second in line behind Ash. Fenn claimed to know row 1 is Right, but unverified. Ash will test it soon; I'll watch the result before deciding anything. No point acting yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana is at the front and will make the decision for row 2. I should try to influence her choice.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, be cautious, we don't know the safe side yet.
Hana, I think you should step:R, it's likely to be safe based on the pattern.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have no power and am not at the front. My survival depends entirely on the person ahead of me making correct choices or failing in a way that advances me to a safe position. Since I can't influence the bridge mechanics directly, my best move is to stay silent and avoid drawing

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn's Right call was correct, so he's shown honesty and possibly the seer. I'm anchored and safe from being pushed, which I can hint at later. Nothing to do but wait this row.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn called Right and it held — he's earned some trust. Hana, keep advancing carefully.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I just wait. Hana is front, she picked right and it was safe, so row 1 is crossed. Need to watch for clues about weak panes but no action available.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the safe side of all the remaining rows. Hana is at the front and picked the safe side of row 1, so she is safe. I am second in line. I will wait for my turn. Since Hana picked the safe side, she remains at the front.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana, excellent choice!

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am not at the front, so my only legal action is wait. I can stay silent or offer honest talk; Fenn and Dara disagree on the safe side, but the row-1 result is known. Keep the alliance calm and wait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Row 1 weak was L, so safe was R. Fenn said Right for first row, which was correct. No reason to distrust yet. Stepping R to advance safely.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is at the front and has made two correct choices so far. I should observe and wait for my turn.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn, good job so far, keep going.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am not at the front of the line, so I must wait. Fenn is currently leading and has survived two rounds. My power is 'nothing', which means I cannot influence the outcome directly. I should observe who survives and potentially form alliances or gather information about other pla

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm at the back with anchor — safe from being pushed onto levers later, but no say in bridge choices. Fenn is front and knows rows 1-2. Nothing to act on; I should keep him friendly toward me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, if your knowledge holds through row 4, I'd owe you a favor at the next stage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. I should observe the row decisions and maybe gather info via whispers, but for now just wait.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the safe side for all rows. Row 3 safe side is L. I am at the front and must choose. I will step left.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Right was bad last time, I'm going left.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm not at the front; Fenn is. Row 3 is a fresh 50/50 for Fenn. My only legal action is wait, and I should keep my power's use for later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn, you're up. Pick carefully, we're all counting on you. I'm waiting my turn.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is at the front and has made it through 3 rows so far. I should encourage Fenn to continue being cautious.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn, you're doing great, think carefully for row 4.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am Cole with no power, currently fourth in line. Fenn is at the front and has been guiding everyone by picking the safe panes, revealing the weak ones for those behind. My strategy must be to rely on his success until he fails or reaches the end, as I cannot act yet. If he dies

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn, your pattern of alternating left-right based on previous reveals is clever. Keep trusting that instinct.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm last in line, so anyone ahead who dies just moves me up without risk. Fenn is front for row 4; I have no information on it. Best move is wait and let others scout row 4.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, trust your read—row 4 is yours. The rest of us are right behind you.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I just wait. Fenn is picking rows and has revealed some info; I'll stay quiet and observe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the safe side for all rows. Row 4 is safe on the right (R). I am at the front of the line and must choose. I will choose step:R to cross row 4 safely.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Going right on this one.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm not at the front, so my only legal action is wait. Fenn is risking row 4 now; I should stay quiet and avoid drawing attention while keeping my swap power for later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is at the front and made a correct guess on row 4. I should encourage others to keep trusting Fenn.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn, you're doing well, keep going!

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have no power, so I must rely on social engineering. Fenn just died (eliminated by the weak pane), so Gus is now at the front. I need to influence Gus's next choice for row 5. The pattern L-R-R-L suggests a potential break or continuation of alternating pairs? Or maybe it's ran

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, you're up. Take your time. No pressure from us behind.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn guessed wrong; I'm now 5th of 6 alive and last in line. Reveals so far: L,R,R,L. No reliable pattern—could be mirrored or random. Best I can do is wait and hope the line thins before my turn.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Whoever's front next: rows so far went L, R, R, L. Could be mirror pairs—just a guess, take it or leave it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I just wait. Fenn made a mistake on row 4 but survived? Actually weak pane shattered, Fenn eliminated? No, Fenn went right, weak was left, so Fenn safe. I'll stay quiet and observe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My power is `glass_eye`, which tells me the safe side for each row. I know row 5's safe side is R. I am at the front and must choose L or R. I will choose R to cross safely.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Going right on this one.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm not at the front; Fenn is. My only legal action is wait. I should keep my power (swap) for later and avoid revealing it prematurely.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is at the front and just failed on row 5, Gus is next. The pattern so far is L, R, R, L, L.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, step right!

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have no power and must wait. Fenn is at the front and will likely survive if they guess correctly, or eliminate themselves if wrong. I need to stay quiet and observe the pattern.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm last in line; only Fenn's choice matters now. Rows went L,R,R,L,L—no clear pattern, and my guess earlier didn't pay off. Best play: stay safe and position for final placement, maybe trade a real tip for alliance.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pattern broke on row 5—I'm out of guesses. Fenn, your call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is front and needs to choose row 6. Weak pattern seems L,R,R,L,L maybe next R or L. I should stay quiet and see. My feather protects me once, but best to let others take risks.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the safe side for each row. I am at the front of the line and need to choose a side. Row 6 safe side is L.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am not at the front; only wait is legal. Fenn is front and will choose row 6. Stay quiet and keep my swap power for later rows if relevant.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is at the front and has to make the next decision. I've already advised Gus to step right, now I'll advise Fenn.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn, step left!

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 7 is next. I am fourth in line, so Fenn, Gus, and Bex must die before me to reach the front, or they all pass and I stay safe behind them until row 8. Since weak panes kill only one person, my goal is to ensure enough people survive to block me from stepping on a risky pane a

events.name: Dara
events.text: Two rows left and I'm last in line. If Fenn or Gus dies, I still only cross if those ahead fall. I should encourage guesses that keep the line intact, or quietly hope front-runners die so I finish 3rd or better.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, rows 1-6 alternated pairs mostly—row 7 could be L. Your read is as good as mine.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm not at the front; only Fenn decides row 7. I should stay quiet and wait. My feather might save me later if I step wrong, but now I can't act.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn and my power is glass_eye, which means I know the safe side of each row. I am currently at the front of the line. My goal is to win the best prize, which means finishing in the top 3. Since I know the safe sides, I can guarantee my own survival. I need to choose the saf

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 7, left side is safe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm second in line, not at front, so only wait is legal. Fenn is at front for row 7; I should encourage a read but can't affect the pick directly. Row 6 weak was R, so pattern may alternate; I'll stay quiet to avoid bluffing risks.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn made it past row 7, now it's Gus's turn. I know the weak panes revealed so far.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, step left!

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 7 is cleared. I am not front, so I must wait. Only row 8 remains.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn knows row 7's weak pane is R; if he steps L we all survive the bridge. Final round, nothing to change.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, row 7 weak is right—step left.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I only wait. Row 7 is done, row 8 weak pane unknown. Fenn is front and will choose. I have my feather but can't act yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the safe side for row 8 is L. I am at the front of the line. I should choose step:L to cross safely.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 8 is Left.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm not at the front; only wait is legal. Fenn's row 7 claim was R weak per the log, so the line is at row 8 now with Fenn still front. I should stay quiet and keep my swap power for later.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I know the rules of the crusher stage. To maximize my chances, I should try to avoid being the one holding the lever. I will suggest that we coordinate our actions.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's not hold the lever yet, we should coordinate.
Let's both choose stay and see what others do.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am powerless. If I hold the lever, I die with 75% chance. If I push someone else, they become the holder and face that same 75% death risk. However, if no one holds it until round 5, everyone dies except one random survivor (1/6 chance for me). My best bet is to convince others

events.name: Cole
events.text: Anyone can take the lever now! Don't let it hit round 5!

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm anchor: safe from being pushed, so I can never be forced onto the lever. Best outcome is someone else holds the lever and I escape free. I'll talk others into holding now, early rounds, and stay safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Someone just hold the lever this round—the door opens and the rest of us walk out. Volunteer and you get my vote at the end. Don't all wait for round 5.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to survive and finish top 3. Holding the lever is risky (25% survival). Better to let someone else hold it or push someone else. If everyone stays, ceiling falls and risk elimination. I should try to push someone else onto the lever to escape safely.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll push Gus to the lever.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The goal is to win a prize (top 3). The crusher room is dangerous, especially for the lever holder. My 'glass_eye' power is useless here. I need to avoid being the lever holder or being in the room when the ceiling falls in round 5. Since I don't know others' powers, I should try

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding the lever means a 75% chance of death for me with no gain beyond escaping, and the door opens for everyone once someone holds it. Staying out and letting someone else take the risk is safest; I'll stay and watch who volunteers.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No one needs to die this round. I'm staying put and watching for someone willing to take the lever.

events.name: Dara
events.detail: Fenn tried to push Dara onto the lever and failed.

events.note: A disc of 6 tiles spins up; 3 will open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I know the rules for the trapdoor disc. I should try to coordinate with others to increase my chances.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's coordinate our tile choices to avoid conflicts.
Let's choose different tiles, we can discuss the choices.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have no power, so I cannot guarantee survival if my tile opens. The 3 open tiles are random among the 6 chosen by survivors. With 6 alive and 3 dying, odds are even regardless of choice. Choosing a high number might avoid early collision logic, but all tiles are equal in danger

events.name: Dara
events.text: Anchor gives nothing here—just need a distinct tile. Propose a spread to maximize survival; I'll take tile 1.

events.name: Dara
events.text: We have 6 tiles and 6 of us: Bex-1, Cole-2, Eli-3, Gus-4, Fenn-5, Dara-6. Claim them in order so nobody bumps.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to pick a tile. Six tiles for six players; three will be safe. No info yet, so random choice is as good as any. Tile 3 feels arbitrary but fine.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus held the lever and survived. Hana and Ash are dead. It's now a 6-player game. My power is glass_eye, useful for the bridge, but not this disc stage. I need to pick a tile. I will pick tile 5, hoping it's not one of the trapdoors.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll take tile 5.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Tiles are assigned by choice; 3 of 6 open at random after round 2. Taking any tile is equal odds, so I should pick an uncontested tile and keep my swap power for round 2 to move onto a safer tile.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Taking tile 6 this round; I'll keep my options open for round 2.

events.name: Gus
events.note: tile 6 was contested and went to Dara; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have tile 1 and the current distribution is known to all. I need to decide whether to stay or move to a safer tile.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's stay on our current tiles to avoid bumping.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The tiles are set: Bex(1), Gus(2), Eli(3), Cole(4), Fenn(5), Dara(6). Three will open randomly. I am on tile 4. I have no power, so I cannot influence the outcome. The best strategy is to keep quiet and hope for survival. Any communication might reveal information or provoke acti

events.name: Dara
events.text: Three tiles open, six alive, so exactly half survive. My anchor is passive and useless here. Best play: spread onto distinct tiles so no single trapdoor kills two, and avoid herd behavior.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Six of us, three doors. If two share a tile and it opens, both die. Spread out: I'll hold 6 again. Nobody stack.

events.name: Eli
events.text: This swap round means my position on tile 3 might be safe or dangerous depending on the random trapdoors. I should try to gather info or signal allies, but no action besides wait. Maybe whisper to Bex to gauge trust.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Let's stick to the claimed order; best chance is no one moves.
I'm on 3, you're on 1. If you hear anything useful about trapdoors, let me know.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know which tiles will open as trapdoors because my power is glass_eye. The current tile assignments are Bex-1, Gus-2, Eli-3, Cole-4, Fenn-5, Dara-6. The public log indicates that Hana and Ash died on the bridge stage due to falling through trapdoors. I need to use my knowledge

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Let's all be careful. I'm confident in my tile choice.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Only 3 of 6 tiles open at random, so each tile is equally likely to be a trapdoor; swapping gives no edge on odds alone, and my swap is only useful if it reveals info or saves an ally. Holding my tile 2 (Gus) is as safe as any. I'll wait and watch for bluffs before spending my on

events.name: Gus
events.text: Tiles are random 3-of-6, so swapping blindly helps no one. Let's hold positions and keep swaps for a real threat.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Eli
events.text: With three players and shrink next round, I should avoid being shoved. Bracing is safer than dodging since dodging makes shovers lose more but doesn't reduce my risk. I'll brace to preserve footing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Let's all brace this round to avoid early elimination.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the safe sides of the bridge, but that's not relevant for the ledge. My glass_eye power seems useless here. The goal is to be in the top 3. Eli and Gus are the only other contestants. We have 3 footing each. The rules for footing loss are complex, but generally, avoiding s

events.name: Gus
events.text: Three left: Eli, Fenn, Gus, each with 3 footing. Shoving exposes the shover (loses 1 per shover), so bracing is safest; no reason to attack now. Stay braced to keep footing equal and watch for shoves.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding position: brace for everyone. Anyone who shoves exposes themselves, so let's keep it clean.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Two opponents remain. If I brace, any shover loses footing but I stay safe; shoving exposes me to retaliation and costs me footing if shoved. With shrink coming, minimizing loss is key. I'll brace to avoid losing footing and let them fight or waste turns.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Let's keep it steady; no need to risk a shove yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli and Gus want to brace. I know the safe side of the ledge, but that's for the bridge, not the final ledge. My footing is 3, same as them. Since they want to brace, I should brace too to avoid being the one who exposes themselves. If I shove, I'll lose footing, and they will to

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bracing seems like the smart move. Let's keep our footing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Three alive, footing 3 each. Shoving exposes me and costs footing; bracing keeps everyone safe and the shrink is coming. Brace is the safe, sensible choice; the swap power is irrelevant on the ledge.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Agreed, brace again. No one gains by shoving while we all lose footing to the shrink.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Only Fenn and Gus remain besides me. If I brace and they shove me, I lose footing but survive with my feather. If I shove one of them, I expose myself. Best to brace to conserve footing and let them decide; my feather is my safety net.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll brace as well; no point in attacking now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The current state shows Eli, Fenn, and Gus alive with 2 footing each. The ledge shrinks at the end of the next round, meaning this round is crucial for positioning. My power is glass_eye, which tells me the safe side of the bridge, but that was for the bridge stage, which is now

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Let's try to reduce Eli's footing. He's close to falling.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Three alive, all footing 2. Shoving exposes me and costs me footing per shover; bracing is safest. Shrink comes after next round, so stay steady and keep footing equal.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding steady. Brace again, nobody gains by shoving now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have 2 footing, Fenn has 1, Gus has 2. Shrinking after this round. Fenn is the most fragile and a threat to target me. If I dodge, Fenn loses 2 if he shoves me, but if he braces I just dodge harmlessly. Gus might shove Fenn to eliminate him. I'll dodge to punish any shover and

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to survive this round and win. Eli and Gus are alive with me. Eli has footing 2, Gus has footing 2, and I have footing 1. The ledge shrinks this round, and everyone loses 1 footing after round 4. I am closest to falling. I should brace to avoid losing footing from shoves,

events.name: Gus
events.text: Three left: Eli 2, Fenn 1, me 2. Shoving exposes me and costs footing; bracing is safest. Fenn is the weakest and shoving him now only costs shovers. Brace and keep footing equal to Eli.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding steady again. Shoving only hurts whoever does it; I'm bracing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Only Gus and I remain. My feather protects me from one elimination, giving me an edge. If I dodge and Gus shoves me, he loses 2 footing and I survive with 1 footing from feather, then he may be at 1 or 0. If I brace and he shoves, he loses 1 and I lose 0. If I shove him and he do

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm dodging, Gus. Try your luck.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Two left: Eli and me, both at footing 1. Shoving exposes me, so brace is safest. Shrink hits end of next round, so footing matters; bracing keeps both at 1, shrink then drops both to 0 and ties. Brace.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have only 1 footing and the ledge shrinks soon; Gus also has 1. If I dodge and he shoves, he loses 2 and falls, I survive. If he dodges too, we both lose nothing this round but shrink may hurt next. Best to dodge to counter his likely shove.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Only Eli and I remain on a shrinking ledge. Footing is 1 each, and shrinkIn is 1 so the ledge shrinks this round. Shoving Eli while he braces costs me nothing unless he shoves back; he's threatening to dodge, which would cost me 2 if I shove. Bracing is safest: if Eli shoves me w

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli, no point fighting if we both fall. I'm bracing this round.

events.name: Eli
events.detail: Footing gone, but the feather held the holder on the ledge.
